The upstream BFCL tree is represented by its tracked-path capture, empty status capture, and per-file digest closure. Unmaterialized upstream file bytes and repository metadata were not accessed.
No Runtime endpoint, socket, provider, model completion, test label, raw benchmark sidecar, environment secret, network resource, or path outside this bundle was accessed.

findings.rationale: The fixed case manifest predates result access, but its execution identity is not one internally consistent worker closure. It separately pins the final pyproject at SHA-256 3f0c2341bf8a58274e23599ef2e821f44a87c326a48205fe9923f9d5a78ef69 while pinning worker-closure candidate.4.7, whose own environment section records pyproject SHA-256 2acedb65f0241836c28102df2fb7c71521a45012c45644dce32c52dc7cb51eaf and whose captures contain the pre-fix 209-test run without explicit configuration. The semantically closed final environment is candidate.4.10 with the 211-test explicit-config captures, but it is not the preregistered dependency closure. The scorer checks the composite component hashes without requiring the referenced closure's internal source/config identities to equal the separately pinned materials.
findings.required_action: Before any BFCL result access, freeze a successor execution identity and case manifest whose worker closure is the exact final candidate.4.10 source/config/wheel environment. Validate that the closure's internal pyproject, lock, wheel, adapter, runner-root, and capture identities equal the separately pinned components, then bind or rerun every per-case receipt against that coherent preregistration.
findings.title: BFCL preregistration pins a composite stale worker environment

findings.rationale: The fixed-path global capability and 24-slot ledger close the caller-selected-ledger defect, but the sole executor still accepts an arbitrary caller-supplied provider_call callable and invokes it once. The ledger therefore proves one callback invocation per slot, not one provider request: the callable can issue zero, one, or multiple completion requests before returning. No sealed adapter or independently replayable provider-acceptance receipt constrains its internal effects. Consequently the implementation does not enforce an aggregate ceiling of exactly 24 actual T2 model calls.
findings.required_action: Keep the fixed authorization, ledger, latch, and global capability paths, but move provider access into a sealed sole adapter that can issue exactly one request for one preallocated slot. Bind a provider-native acceptance or request receipt per slot so the append-only ledger accounts for actual provider requests, and add adversarial tests proving callbacks or multiple executor objects cannot exceed 24 aggregate calls.
findings.title: The bootstrap boundary limits callbacks, not actual provider requests

findings.rationale: The immutable bundle was created at 2026-08-22T04:24:47.605158+00:00 and the REVIEW_REQUIRED ledger entries were recorded around 2026-08-22T04:24:39+00:00. Those entries cite an amendment declared effective at 2026-08-22T12:50:00+08:00, while the BFCL execution identity and case manifest declare freeze times of 12:30 and 13:00 +08:00. The bytes existed before result access, but the ledger and preregistration metadata assert legal-effect or freeze times later than records that already depend on them. This prevents the ledger from being a temporally truthful single state source.
findings.required_action: Use actual immutable creation and effective times. Append post-effective stage transitions rather than back-referencing a not-yet-effective amendment, regenerate the checkpoint from those entries, and freeze the BFCL identity and case manifest with timestamps that truthfully precede dependent records and all result access.
findings.title: Stage and preregistration records rely on future-effective timestamps

findings.rationale: The R1 AUTHOR_CANDIDATE ledger entry asserts the active full-source root c6a4aa566c95513414a567a0e6299d37dab8a8bbee9c507c0e479d894a39f190, but its bound contract-validation receipt embeds a different 16-entry candidate.4 source inventory rooted at cd64dd701424a0adac7a30fa1032b220347c38d4edc2fb709eec84ed33c862a7. The ledger validator checks the asserted source-root field and receipt hash but does not reconcile the receipt's internal source identity. The R1 authored state is therefore attributed to source bytes that its own receipt does not validate.
findings.required_action: Regenerate the R1 contract-validation receipt from the complete active 392-entry source inventory, require stage-ledger reconciliation to compare each receipt's internal candidate and source identity with the ledger entry, then append a successor R1 authored/review-required chain and checkpoint.
findings.title: The R1 stage receipt embeds a stale source inventory

parent_finding_closures.rationale: Authorization is reconstructed from fixed, content-addressed receipts and identities; a caller-supplied approval object is rejected.
The importer recomputes the closed bundle, raw xhigh process/event/output hashes, authority, boundary, source identity, and semantic review conditions before emitting receipts.
Any REVISE result emits no receipts. ACCEPTED requires two independent outputs, all three stages accepted, all parent findings closed, and zero open P0/P1.
Claims, receipts, source closure, candidate identity, and stage state are explicitly bound; historical candidate.2 evidence remains qualified and non-authorizing.

The attempt ledger is append-only, fsync-backed, hash-chained, slot-bound, terminal-finalized, and revalidates legal snapshots. The remaining actual-provider-call boundary defect is reported separately as DG10-C4-AI-021.
The Runtime wheel is content-addressed, the retained rebuild is byte-identical, and the final report closes the executed source/config/capture set.
The authorization graph has a reachable exact-24 bootstrap state after bound R0-R2 acceptance while continuing to deny test and release. Residual call-time enforcement is separately open.
Test access requires a separate two-audit artifact importer with exact denominators and a one-use fixed-path executor; release and controlled-decision entry points fail closed.

The manifest predates result access, but its execution identity combines the final pyproject with a worker closure that internally binds the pre-fix pyproject and captures. It is not the exact coherent final worker environment required by the superseding candidate.4.4 action.
The current serving gate is inert and fail-closed; any successor gate is rebuilt from fixed raw receipts plus the reconciled attempt ledger with coverage, identity, uniqueness, and window checks.
The schema and importer require AI authority, model/process truthfulness, closed-set boundary facts, raw-run binding, and conditional disposition rather than a human-review representation.

All six R0-R2 entries are materialized and hash-chained, and the checkpoint exactly replays current states. The receipt-source and timestamp contradictions are separately reported as DG10-C4-AI-022 and DG10-C4-AI-023.
The active aggregate is replayed from both immutable raw xhigh audit attempts, their receipts, distinct thread identities, stage receipts, bundle receipt, and checkpoint.
A dedicated raw-artifact test-access importer binds two distinct xhigh audits and exact inputs, while the fixed-path executor enforces one-use consumption before callback invocation.

The superseding action is implemented: authorization binds fixed active ledger and latch paths, a candidate-global capability is atomically consumed, alternative paths are unavailable, and duplicate executors are rejected. The distinct callback-versus-provider-request bypass is DG10-C4-AI-021.
The final executed closure includes and verifies the previously missing migration template.
The immutable amendment changes only max to xhigh, records the interrupted max process as non-authorizing, and all active audit import checks require gpt-5.6-sol with xhigh reasoning.
The independently rebuilt wheel is retained and byte-identical to the source wheel at SHA-256 882b2f9d13fb16a2a756c21e73d3758789c1f5084129cdef3ae349ca4c8cb773.
Full-test approval is consumed atomically at a fixed path before the access callback; any second or failed consumption remains denied.
The final captures explicitly pass -c evals/dg10/pyproject.toml and --rootdir ., collect and pass 211 tests, and run Ruff with the explicit DG-10 configuration.
